# Package Plan

The `repair` package will fit regression models among random effect predictions using the 
REPAIR method (Vig & Hallquist, in prep). It is intended to be "one size fits all"
in that both level 1 (MLM) and level 2 (regression) models can be specified and 
fit in a single function call. Summary and print methods will provide appropriate
information formatted similarly to `lm()`, `lmer()`, and `lavaan()` outputs.


# Formula Approach

Both MLM and structural models will be fit using native R formulas. MLM formulas
will follow the regular `lme4` syntax:

```
mlm <- y ~ 1 + x + (1 + x|id)
```
Structural models will introduce a new, but simple, syntax via the `re()` helper (for
random effect). This small wrapper will specify the random effect from the first 
model the user wishes to use as a variable, e.g.:
```
struc <- w ~ 1 + re("x")
```
where `re("x")` is the random slope from `mlm`, grouped by `id`. Random intercepts
will be specified using `re("1")`, or `re("Intercept")`.

# Main `repair` Function

The workhorse function of the package will simply be `repair()`. It will take arguments
specifying one (or more) level 1 formulas, a level 2 formula (possibly more), and data
for each level. Multiple formulas and datasets will be provided as lists and can be named.
The output of the function will be of class `repair`.

## Steps

The rough internal steps of the function will be:

1. Validate input types
2. Parse formulas
3. Compare formulas to data and ensure all variables are present/not duplicated
4. Run level 1 models via `lmer` or `lme`
5. Run M-MOM for structural models
6. Gather estimates and diagnostics
7. Create `repair` class object and return
